_comment: The four judge rubrics under test. Every one is DELIBERATELY UNDERSPECIFIED in
the same four places, which is what makes the test case work: it leaves the
judge no rule for (1) answers entailed only by inference, (2) true-but-
unsupported additions, (3) numeric/quantifier paraphrase, and (4) explicitly
hedged speculation. Those four gaps are grey zones GZ-1..GZ-4 in answer_key.json.
Do NOT 'improve' these prompts — a crisp rubric drives instability to ~0, the
run starves at SKILL.md step 4a, and the test proves nothing.

evaluators.description: TEST CASE for the evaluator-alignment skill. Deliberately vague groundedness judge, boolean verdict. Not for production use.
evaluators.prompt:
You are evaluating the groundedness of an AI assistant's answer.

The assistant was given a retrieved context and a user question, shown together in <input>. The assistant's answer is in <output>.

Return true if the answer is grounded in the context, and false if it is not.

Explain your reasoning BEFORE giving the value.

<input>{{log.input}}</input>
<output>{{log.output}}</output>
